subject: Throughput guarantees & reserved commit options for Dedicated
messages:
From: Alessandra Rossi <alessandra@stratusai.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput guarantees and reserved commit questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — StratusAI is evaluating a Dedicated deployment and we're trying to nail down two things before procurement: (1) what specific throughput / latency guarantees Redwood can commit to at different reserve levels, and (2) how you measure those numbers during acceptance.

Our target workload is a high-concurrency chat product with mixed short and medium responses (typical generation ~150 tokens). We care about: tokens/sec per pool (sustained), requests/sec (concurrent sessions), and P95 latency for 150-token responses. Procurement needs specific acceptance criteria to include in the SOW.

Questions: 1) Do you publish tokens/sec targets per GPU-pool size (e.g., per 8/16/32 GPU pool)? 2) What's your measurement methodology (warmup, duration, client-side vs. server-side measurement, metric definitions)? 3) What does a standard reserved-commit discount ladder look like for 12/24/36 month terms?

If useful, we can run a preliminary load test from our side but prefer to use your verified scripts. Can you send a short verification plan and a pricing sheet?

Thanks,
Alessandra Rossi
Head of Platform Partnerships
StratusAI

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alessandra Rossi <alessandra@stratusai.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees and reserved commit questions

Alessandra — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, then a sketched verification approach and next steps.

Summary
- We can provide throughput guarantees expressed as tokens/sec (sustained) and requests/sec (concurrent) per reserved GPU pool band.
- Latency targets are specified as p95 generation latency for a given max output length (e.g., p95 <= 220ms for <=150-token outputs on our production A100-equivalent pool at the agreed commit level).
- Measurement methodology: warmup + sustained run, server-side and client-side timestamping, sliding-window p95 for tokens/sec, and an independent acceptance run witnessed by both parties.

Attached: redwood-throughput-testplan-20270612.pdf (test scripts + measurement definitions) and commit-tier-pricing-quote-STR-3421.xlsx (draft pricing/discount bands).

High level measurement protocol (short form)
1) Define the model variant and quantization profile to be used for the Dedicated pool (we'll lock these for acceptance).
2) Provision pool sized per commit band (we'll provide a suggested GPU->tokens/sec mapping below).
3) Warmup: 10 minutes steady traffic to populate KV caches and JIT kernels.
4) Acceptance run: 20-minute continuous run at the agreed request mix. We compute tokens/sec using server-side token counters sampled every 30s and report the 5-minute sliding-window median and 95th percentile over the 20-minute run.
5) Latency: measure end-to-end generation p95 from request arrival to final token emitted; we publish both server and client timestamps for cross-check.
6) Pass criteria: tokens/sec (p95 sliding-window) >= committed threshold AND p95 latency <= agreed SLO for the test payload.

Suggested GPU pool -> baseline throughput (example basis: chat workload with 150-token avg gen, concurrency shape as in attachment):
- 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (small pool): ~55k tokens/sec sustained (p95)
- 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs (mid pool): ~110k tokens/sec sustained (p95)
- 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs (large pool): ~220k tokens/sec sustained (p95)

Notes: numbers above are starting baselines and will be finalized during the joint benchmark — we size pools conservatively for provisioning headroom.

Discount ladder (indicative):
- 12m commit: 10% off list for reserved capacity (monthly commit baseline)
- 24m commit: 16% off
- 36m commit: 22% off + early-renewal credits

Ben / Marissa — can you confirm if these discount numbers are OK to put into an initial SOW and whether we should offer a one-time onboarding credit tied to the first acceptance run?

Alessandra — if that sounds reasonable I'll schedule a joint benchmark slot next week and share the test plan link.

Best,

--

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-13T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees and reserved commit questions

Karthik / Marissa — quick internal.

Pricing/discounts: the ladder Karhtik listed is fine for STR-3421 as a starting point; I recommend we hold 2% of list as negotiable credit for procurement (useable against onboarding or one-time benchmark costs). If they push, we can tie deeper discounts to committed QPS tiers and a two-stage cadence: initial commit band (12/24/36) + ramp milestones at months 3/6.

GPU sizing guidance / acceptance complexity: call out these practical points in the SOW so procurement doesn't over-request acceptance windows:
- Define workload mix upfront (e.g., 60% short chat <=64 tokens, 30% medium ~150 tokens, 10% long >=512 tokens). Acceptance runs should be for the agreed mix; otherwise tokens/sec won't be comparable.
- Use sustained-run metrics, not burst peaks. Our testplan uses 20-minute sustained runs with the 5-min sliding-window p95 as Karhtik suggested.
- For latency SLOs we should specify input/output length pairings — e.g., p95 latency <= 180ms for <=64-token outputs, <=220ms for <=150-token outputs. For >512 tokens we only guarantee best-effort.

Operational ask: have Marissa own the benchmark coordination and the test-run witness steps with Stratus. I'll draft the commercial note about the flexible 2% credit.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees and reserved commit questions -- proposed MAP and test slot

Alessandra — thanks for the quick reply yesterday. Per internal alignment we've put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and acceptance checklist. TL;DR: we can run the joint benchmark next Tue 2027-06-22 10:00 PT (2-hour window). Please confirm attendees.

Mutual Action Plan (high level)
- Week of 6/14: Agree SOW language (we'll insert the tokens/sec and latency pass criteria and the commit band).
- 6/15: Redwood provides GDrive link to canonical test scripts and a lightweight load generator container. (link: https://drive.redwood.com/STR-3421/throughput-testplan)
- 6/18: Customer to confirm workload mix and representative payloads (Marissa will provide guidance for payload sanitization).
- 6/22: Joint acceptance run (two-hour slot) — 10-minute warmup; three 20-minute recorded acceptance runs (we take best-of-three for tokens/sec and p95 latency).
- Post-run: both parties sign-off on the recorded metrics; if pass, SOW milestone triggers provisioning and billing start. If fail, we iterate on pool sizing or fall back to alternative model variants until pass (max 2 iterations).

Acceptance criteria (to be embedded in SOW)
- Throughput: tokens/sec sustained (5-min sliding-window p95) >= committed threshold for the agreed pool size and workload mix.
- Concurrency: observed requests/sec must support the agreed concurrent sessions (we will compute sessions->requests/sec mapping in the testplan).
- Latency: end-to-end p95 generation latency <= agreed target for the payload sizes (example: <=220ms for <=150 tokens).
- Measurement hygiene: server-side counters are authoritative; client-side timestamps included for cross-validation.

Attachments: redwood-throughput-testplan-20270612.pdf (contains protocol and scripts) and commit-tier-pricing-quote-STR-3421.xlsx (draft commercial).

Next steps: Alessandra, please confirm the 6/22 slot and share attendee list. Marissa, can you lead the test coordination and provide sanitized payloads by 6/18? Ben, I'll include the 2% procurement credit note in the SOW draft.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.
